pages.text: "Even higher!" Lulu stacked olives on a stone in the yard. The tower reached Lulu's nose. Beside the stone, the baby cousin watched from a blanket.
The baby stretched out a forepaw. Crash! The whole olive tower fell. "Go away! It is my tower!" Lulu shouted.
The baby pouted, then cried. Three cousins stepped back, startled. Lulu's ears lay flat back. The yard fell quiet.
Mom set down the olive basket and sat beside Lulu. "Your ears are flat back." Lulu touched them with a forepaw. They really were.
"Ears down means anger. Anger drifts away after a little while." Mom put a hand on her tummy. "Breathe in deeply, then out long." Lulu filled the tummy and breathed out too.
Oh! The flattened ears slowly stood up again. "Ears down? Breathe out!" Lulu touched them and smiled. The yard seemed bright again.
Lulu crouched before the crying baby. "Sorry I shouted. My falling tower upset me." The baby stopped crying and grabbed Lulu's bell. Jingle!
Three cousins came back to gather olives. All four built a taller tower. Lulu's ears stood high, mouth open in a smile.
The baby reached again. Lulu's ears began to drop. "One, touch your ears! Two, breathe out! Three, say you are upset!" Lulu gently held the baby's hand. "Touch this, and it falls."
Mom hugged Lulu and the baby together. Breathe out to let anger go. Ears down? Breathe out! "Now I will build you a tower too." Lulu set olives before the baby.
